name.text: Relations Q2 - Mapping type for f(x) = x squared

questiontext.text:
Consider the function \(f(x) = x^2\), defined for all real numbers \(x\). What type of mapping does this function represent?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To classify a mapping, ask two questions. Does any input have more than one output? Can two different inputs share the same output?

Each real number \(x\) has exactly one square, so every input has exactly one output. The mapping is a function, and so it cannot be one-to-many or many-to-many.

Now try \(x = 2\) and \(x = -2\): \(f(2) = 4\) and \(f(-2) = (-2)^2 = 4\). Two different inputs give the same output. The same happens for every non-zero number and its negative, because \((-x)^2 = x^2\). On the graph, the horizontal line \(y = 4\) meets the parabola twice.

[[jsxgraph width="320px" height="240px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-4, 9, 4, -1.2], axis: true, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false}); b.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return x*x; }, -3.2, 3.2], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2}); b.create('line', [[-4, 4], [4, 4]], {strokeColor: '#c62828', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2, fixed: true}); b.create('point', [-2, 4], {name: '(-2, 4)', size: 3, color: '#c62828', fixed: true, label: {offset: [-55, 12]}}); b.create('point', [2, 4], {name: '(2, 4)', size: 3, color: '#c62828', fixed: true, label: {offset: [8, 12]}}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Many inputs share one output, so \(f(x) = x^2\) is a many-to-one mapping. It is not one-to-one. The correct answer is B.

questionnote.text: Fixed: f(x)=x^2 on the reals, key B (many-to-one).

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic.

falsefeedback.text: First decide whether each input \(x\) gives one output or several. Then compare \(f(a)\) and \(f(-a)\) for a number such as \(a = 3\): can two different inputs give the same output?
